displayQuote: When they go low, we go high

meta.title: Who really said "When they go low, we go high"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes — Michelle Obama said it, in her own words, at the 2016 Democratic National Convention on 25 July 2016. Her speechwriter confirms the line was hers.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'When they go low, we go high'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified: Michelle Obama coined it at the 2016 DNC (25 July 2016). Her chief speechwriter says the line was Mrs. Obama's own.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: b. 1964 · First Lady of the United States, 2009–2017
answer.sourceLine: Michelle Obama delivered the line in her address to the Democratic National Convention on 25 July 2016: “…our motto is, when they go low, we go high.” The exact wording is preserved in the official White House transcript, and her chief speechwriter says the line was Mrs. Obama’s own.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Remarks by the First Lady at the Democratic National Convention
Michelle Obama, First Lady of the United States

source.excerpt: With every word we utter, with every action we take, we know our kids are watching us. We as parents are their most important role models. And let me tell you, Barack and I take that same approach to our jobs… How we explain that when someone is cruel, or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level — no, our motto is, when they go low, we go high.
trail: The official White House transcript records the exact line: “our motto is, when they go low, we go high.”
Wikiquote catalogs the line under her sourced 2016 Democratic National Convention remarks — not in any “misattributed” or “disputed” section.
Her chief White House speechwriter, Sarah Hurwitz, told reporters “I did not write that line — she came up with it” (The Hill).
source.excerptNote: From the official White House transcript of the address; the line closes a passage about how she and President Obama teach their daughters to answer cruelty.

source.rightsNote: The address was delivered and published in 2016. A First Lady is not a federal employee whose works fall into the public domain under U.S. copyright law, and a partisan convention speech is a personal work — so the text remains under Michelle Obama’s copyright.

author.name: Michelle Obama
author.heading: About Michelle Obama
author.metaLine: b. 1964 · Lawyer, author & First Lady of the United States (2009–2017)
author.bio: Michelle LaVaughn Robinson Obama (born 1964) is an American attorney and author who served as First Lady from 2009 to 2017. A Princeton and Harvard Law graduate, she became one of the most visible and quoted public figures of her era; her 2018 memoir Becoming was a record-breaking bestseller. Her 2016 convention line “when they go low, we go high” became a defining political catchphrase of the decade.

misattribution.heading: Correctly attributed — but note the myths
misattribution.intro: Unusually for a viral one-liner, this one is genuinely the person’s own words. The confusions that circulate are about who authored it and how old it is, not whether she said it.

items.scope: “It’s an old proverb she was quoting.”
items.why: No documented use of the exact phrase predates the 25 July 2016 speech; it is catalogued as her own line, not a quotation, on Wikiquote.
Hurwitz has repeatedly disclaimed authorship: “I did not write that line — she came up with it. My contribution was typing it,” per The Hill.

misattribution.truthLine: The line is authentically Michelle Obama’s, spoken at the 2016 Democratic National Convention and preserved verbatim in the official White House transcript.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Michelle Obama delivered the line while making the case for Hillary Clinton and, without naming him, rebuking the tone of Donald Trump’s campaign. Framed as parenting advice — how she and the President teach their daughters to answer cruelty — it became the emotional center of the 2016 convention and one of the most repeated political phrases of the decade.

She returned to the motto often in later years, including a candid reflection at the 2020 convention that going high is “a hard way to live — but it is the only way.” The phrase has since been printed on posters, shirts, and memes far beyond its original context.
context.pull: “When someone is cruel, or acts like a bully, you don’t stoop to their level.”
